source: NCERT Class VII, Our Pasts II, History Ch. 2.

sections.heading: 1. The Emergence of New Dynasties (c. 7th century)
points: By the **7th century**, big **landlords and warrior chiefs** were recognised by kings as subordinate rulers called **samantas**.
As they gained power and wealth, samantas rose to **maha-samanta / maha-mandaleshvara** and some declared **independence**.

Example: the **Rashtrakutas** (Deccan) — subordinate to the **Chalukyas**; in the mid-8th century **Dantidurga** overthrew his overlord and performed the **hiranya-garbha** ('golden womb') ritual to claim kshatriya status.

sections.heading: 2. Administration and Prashastis
points: Kings adopted grand titles — **maharaja-adhiraja** ('great king, overlord of kings'), **tribhuvana-chakravartin**.
**Prashastis** (praise poems) recorded rulers' achievements, often composed by **learned Brahmanas**.
**Resources** came from peasants, and functionaries were often recruited from **influential families**; positions became **hereditary**.
Kings shared power with **samantas** and with **peasants, traders and Brahmanas**.

sections.heading: 3. Warfare and Kanauj — The Tripartite Struggle
points: For centuries three dynasties fought to control the city of **Kanauj** (Ganga valley) — the **"tripartite struggle"**:
**Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni** (early 11th c.) raided India (incl. the **Somnath temple**); his court poet **Al-Biruni** wrote the **Kitab-ul-Hind** (in Arabic).

sections.heading: 4. The Cholas
points: Rose from the **Kaveri delta**; **Vijayalaya** captured **Thanjavur (Tanjavur)** (mid-9th c.).
**Rajaraja I** (985–1014) — greatest Chola ruler; expanded the empire; built the **Rajarajeshvara (Brihadeshwara) temple** at Thanjavur.
**Rajendra I** — led expeditions to the **Ganga** and across the sea to **Southeast Asia (Srivijaya)**; built a new capital **Gangaikonda-cholapuram**.
Famous **bronze sculptures** (esp. **Nataraja**); temples were centres of craft, trade and religion.

sections.heading: 5. Chola Village Self-Government
points: Rich peasants (**vellalar**) were powerful; settlements of peasants = **ur**; associations = **nadu**.
**Sabha** = assembly of **Brahmana** landholders (in brahmadeya villages); **ur** = assembly of non-Brahmana landowners; **nagaram** = association of **merchants**.
The **Uttaramerur inscriptions** describe how **sabha committees** were chosen by **lot (kudavolai system)** — a remarkable local democracy.

sections.heading: 6. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Samanta → maha-samanta → independent king; Dantidurga (Rashtrakuta) performed hiranya-garbha.
Tripartite struggle for Kanauj: Pratiharas, Palas, Rashtrakutas.
Mahmud of Ghazni raided Somnath; Al-Biruni wrote Kitab-ul-Hind.
Cholas: Vijayalaya (Thanjavur), Rajaraja I (Brihadeshwara temple), Rajendra I (Ganga & SE Asia).
Chola bronzes = Nataraja; village assemblies: sabha (Brahmana), ur, nagaram (merchants); Uttaramerur inscriptions.

sections.heading: 7. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Sabha** = assembly of Brahmana landholders; **ur** = non-Brahmana landowners; **nagaram** = merchants — don't confuse.
The **Brihadeshwara (Rajarajeshvara) temple** was built by **Rajaraja I**, at **Thanjavur**.
**Al-Biruni** (Kitab-ul-Hind) came with **Mahmud of Ghazni**, not Ghori.
Committee members at Uttaramerur were chosen by **lot (kudavolai)**.
